description: Fixture mirror of the Bookly policy graph. Read directly while there is no Neo4j connection. Kept byte-for-byte consistent with seed.cypher: same nodes, same relationships, same property values.
node_key: Each node has a `key` used as the endpoint name in `relationships`. Keys are not stored in Neo4j; the MERGE identity property is noted per node type in seed.cypher.

properties.name: Standard 30-day returns
properties.summary: Physical books may be returned within 30 days of delivery, in resalable condition.

properties.name: Digital purchases are final
properties.summary: Ebooks cannot be returned once the download has been made available.

properties.name: Holiday sale extended returns
properties.summary: Physical books bought during a Bookly holiday sale may be returned within 60 days of delivery instead of 30.

properties.name: Bookly Australia extended returns
properties.summary: A Bookly goodwill extension: customers in Australia get 45 days on physical books instead of 30. This is Bookly's own policy, not a statement about Australian law.

properties.name: Damaged or faulty on arrival
properties.summary: A book that arrived damaged or faulty is returnable even if the window has closed. Needs human review before approval.

notes: DIGITAL_NO_RETURN has no HAS_WINDOW edge and no OVERRIDES edge pointing at it. The absence is the rule: nothing extends a window that does not exist, so no regional or promotional policy can rescue an ebook.
DAMAGED_ON_ARRIVAL does not WAIVE DIGITAL_NO_RETURN either. A faulty ebook is an escalation, not a return.
Precedence is stored twice on purpose: as the `precedence` property (cheap sort) and as OVERRIDES edges (explainable path). The edges are the source of truth for the explanation shown to a customer.
